newsitem.title: UK: Funds turn buyers of Japanese equities - poll.
newsitem.headline: Funds turn buyers of Japanese equities - poll.

text.p: Fund managers globally are looking to add to their holdings of Japanese equities, according to a poll released by Merrill Lynch on Monday.

It said the number of Japanese fund managers bullish on prospects for the Japanese economy rose in February from January and for the second successive month earnings per share estimates were being revised up.
For the first time since November, domestic managers have turned net buyers of Japanese equities, while outside Japan, the sharpest increase in interest came from U.S. and U.K. fund managers.
"On Japanese equities, a positive consensus is developing among fund managers across the globe. We tend to agree with the positive sentiment," Merrill global strategist Bijal Shah said.
In its survey of Japanese fund managers, it noted a sharp reversal with managers turning net buyers of Japanese equities for the first time since November.
On a three month view, bulls outnumbered bears by seven percent, it said.

They were also now buyers of U.S. equities, and were keen on continental European and Asian equities. The poll said fund managers in Japan were reducing cash and selling domestic bonds, although they were buyers of bonds outside the country.
The survey was carried out on February 3 and 4 by Gallup. It covered 43 institutions responsible for funds totally $603 billion.
